checks.observed: The pre-React authorship banner and case/current-study exits render above the dashboard. The audit identifies authored rows and defines its 50% ratio as two mentions among four examples. The generated draft says its business claims and comparison evidence are not supplied. Retest shows 50/100 and 50% on both sides, Not collected provider outcomes, two illustrative position-two rows and two omissions. No ranking improvement is asserted.
checks.result: Observed this complete audit/draft/retest path; other dashboard views and narrow layouts remain open

checks.observed: Default context submits to explicitly authored observations. The draft view shows original and editable proposed text, an unverified source boundary and no-publication message. Entering text and approving shows local revision 1 with the exact entered text. Undo shows revision 2 with the original text still visibly displayed, removes the spent undo control and announces that no website changed.
checks.result: Observed approval and visible one-step rollback; changed-context preservation is separately covered by DOM contracts, not claimed as a browser observation

checks.observed: Each of the four presets updated brand, industry, competitors and question together. Manually edited brand/question became a custom context. Choosing another preset displayed a replacement choice without changing those edits; Keep retained them. Explicit Apply replaced all fields and returned focus to Brand. Context review received heading focus and displayed all four normalized fields before execution. Confirming produced an authored audit for that context. Editing the question then removed that result and review, retained the new question and returned to custom context. In the final focus regression check, editing Industry while the replacement choice was open dismissed that choice, preserved the complete typed value including a subsequent “ today”, and left focus in Industry.
checks.result: Observed desktop preset/context workflow. Full keyboard, narrow-screen, assistive-technology and participant review remain open.

checks.observed: Visited all eight dashboard views. Each displayed a view-specific source explanation and the no-collection/publication boundary; navigation focused the explanation. Expanded definitions describe example scorecards, catalog totals, comparison calculations, source URLs, positions and dates without treating them as real measurements. Citation details explicitly say that source examples were not analyzed by a model. The studio generated an unverified draft. Brand setup stated that it creates a local example without a scrape or provider query; setup was dismissed without creating a workspace.
checks.result: Observed all eight source panels and citation/studio/setup boundaries on desktop. Saved-package classification is covered separately by a source contract, not claimed as a native-browser observation.

checks.version: Archived Aevis URL and note boundaries
checks.observed: A valid URL returned its locally parsed host/path and explicitly unknown HTTP, robots, crawler and indexing status. An invalid URL replaced that feedback with a syntax error and no-fetch statement. A new brand note showed Entered context · unverified and No independent verification, without citation counts. Copy displayed Unverified notes copied. Nothing was published. Switching views and reopening Brand Vault removed the added page-local note as disclosed.
checks.result: Observed these native interactions. Clipboard failure and exact fallback text are covered by handler/helper contracts. This does not certify full keyboard navigation, dialog focus or assistive-technology behavior.

checks.observed: The complete authored baseline rendered 3 / 4 returned fixture responses = 75%, the exact context and no-provider provenance. The condition popup exposed the four other choices once, but subsequent accessibility clicks and keyboard actions left its value at Complete fixture. Alternative result states were not observed.
checks.result: Incomplete browser verification. Keep A13.07 open; passing DOM contracts are not promoted to a browser finding.

checks.version: Original window-and-timeline homepage with project previews
checks.observed: All three featured entries retained the original timeline and short headings. Andalus shows the recovery wireframes and reconstruction caption; Nasaq shows its current conversation, six-icon family, refinement choices and composer with a local-demo caption; Flex shows its saved landing-page headline, supporting panel and primary action. At 300% browser zoom, the narrow Andalus crop focused the changed-fare screen and the Nasaq crop stayed within its frame. The existing footer blur covers content near the lower viewport edge, particularly at high zoom; these crops were inspected by scrolling them into the clearer area. Zoom was restored to 100%. Clicking Nasaq opened its existing language dialog, and closing returned focus to the same Nasaq entry.
checks.result: Observed this desktop preview change and limited high-zoom reflow. Physical mobile, full accessibility, opening-viewport proof and hiring comprehension remain open.

checks.observed: At 300% browser zoom, the fixed footer and its blur no longer cover project content. At the bottom, the optional assistant precedes the two-column footer and all four labels are readable. The boarding action opened its optional interaction; Escape closed it, then restored the same footer button and scroll position after the close transition. Tab proceeded through CV / Resume, WhatsApp and LinkedIn, with visible focus. No contact link was activated. Zoom was restored to 100%.
checks.result: Observed this enlarged homepage and footer path. Real phones, increased system text, all case layouts and full accessibility remain open.

checks.version: Veyra Version 2 recommendation and Version 1 reference
checks.observed: The comparison identifies Version 2 as current and recommended, gives three tasks and labels the earlier Figma sequence Version 1. A legacy style had hidden the disclosure; the scoped override and updated stylesheet reference made the current card, disclosure and scope note visible. Opening the disclosure exposed the saved six-screen reference and its earlier-iteration caption; the Figma flow was not newly evaluated. Following the recommended link opened the current local planner. Its Back to case study link returned to index.html#prototype.
checks.result: Observed the coherent recommended entry, earlier reference disclosure and return destination. No Figma synchronization or traveler improvement is claimed.

checks.version: Veyra current planner desktop keyboard path
checks.observed: From the initial page, Tab reached Skip to place search and Return focused search. Keyboard search found Trevi and the garden; Tab reached each list control, Return opened details and Shift+Tab reached Add. In the first dialog, Escape restored the list opener, and forward/backward Tab wrapped between Close and Add. Two additions produced the same day. Keyboard activation of Review focused its heading and showed both numbered selected pins despite the retained garden search. Earlier moved the garden to stop 1 at 09:30 and Trevi to stop 2 at 11:10. Remove retained Trevi and focused Undo; Return restored the garden in the same order and focused that stop. A fresh final single-add check displayed 1 stop. The case-return link was also observed.
checks.result: Observed the core alternate-control task through change and recovery. Some immediate accessibility snapshots lagged keyboard focus; visible focus was checked before activating the relevant controls. This is a scoped desktop keyboard observation, not a screen-reader or physical-phone certification.
